In May 1542 the Spanish priest Francis Xavier landed at Goa, sent by the king of Portugal. He was one of the founders of the Jesuits, and Goa became the base for Catholic missions across Asia.

The Portuguese had held the town since they seized it in 1510. Xavier did not stay long in one place. He spent years among the Paravar pearl fishers of the Tamil coast, baptising thousands. Then he sailed on:

  • To Malacca and the Spice Islands.
  • To Japan in 1549, the first Jesuit there, a visit recorded as Francis Xavier in Japan.
  • Toward China, but he died in 1552 on an island off the coast before he could enter.

His work had a harsh side. He asked the king to send the Inquisition to Goa, and the Goa Inquisition, set up in 1560, punished converts suspected of keeping Hindu or Jewish ways.

His body was brought back to Goa and lies in the Basilica of Bom Jesus. He is a saint of the Catholic Church, and Jesuit colleges in India still carry his name.
